answer: Per-alias proof of work gates entry: a new alias must solve a unique computational puzzle before it can trade. Each puzzle costs about 6 hours of commodity GPU time, so creating 1,000 aliases costs 6,000 GPU hours and stops cheap mass creation. A public atlas records every alias beside its puzzle solution, and an anchor record links each solution to that alias work history. A nightly echo sweep replays the atlas to catch hollow aliases sharing duplicate or borrowed solutions, and any alias caught is burned and its earnings frozen for 30 days.
